label_equals_title.choice_and_why: Dropping the column rather than blanking the cell: an empty cell under a 'Label' header would read as a missing label; with no Label header nothing is missing. The decision is one boolean (showLabel, line 117) and one conditional at each of the two places the column is drawn. A card that mixes an equal Label and a differing one keeps the column and leaves only the equal cell empty (line 179); the producer emits one value per card, so that case is not one the page receives today. No label is invented from the section id, a slug or anything else.

field_slug_read.denominators: 33 census sections: 17 TYPED, 10 CHART_ONLY, 6 DISCLOSURE; 72 field rows (rows holding a 'field' key); 14 of them lie in the 6 DISCLOSURE sections (including the 2 list and 2 table rows) and are never sections; 58 field rows lie in the 17 TYPED sections with a scalar unit
field_slug_read.producer_rule: infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/ycharts/extract/extract.py (verified by reading the bytes, 2026-10-11): lines 704-707 `sections.append({"section_id": "%s.%s.c%d" % (row["section_id"], _slug(row["field"]), cand["column"]), "section_type": row["section_id"], ...` ; lines 927-928 `def _slug(name): return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "_", str(name).lower()).strip("_")`; lines 211-228 classify_sections and 237-255 census_field_rows (only TYPED sections, only rows with a 'field' key); line 650 a row whose unit is in NON_SCALAR_UNITS ("list", "table", line 113) never becomes a section; line 714 the field name is held privately as _label. The order's 'lines 707-714 and 777' are within three lines of these: 707 is section_type (the code), 714 is _label, 777 is the chart row's units; the chart row's section_id is '<code>.chart.<_slug(section title)>' (line 772), a title slug, not a field slug.
field_slug_read.answer: Yes: the wire's section_id is '<census code>.<slug of the census field name>.c<column>', and section_type is the census code. The slug is a lower-casing with every run of non [a-z0-9] characters collapsed to '_' and trimmed, so it is not reversible by itself; with the code (section_type) it maps back through the census to exactly one field name for every one of the 58 derivable slugs (0 collisions inside a section). The chart rows' slug is a section title, not a field. Nothing was wired into the page; the reviewer rules whether the Label reads the census field name (and whether the page may copy the census's field names, as IV-e-115 copied the 33 titles).
field_slug_read.method: FIELD_SLUG_COUNT.json from field_slug_count.py (this folder, Write-tool authored; run `python -I field_slug_count.py <census> FIELD_SLUG_COUNT.json`). Input: the pinned census alone, docs/briefs/sources/YCHARTS_COMPARISON_REPORT_FIELD_SCRAPE_20260909.json (33 sections), read, not edited. census_fields = rows holding a 'field' key across all 33 sections. slugs_derivable = those rows whose section classifies TYPED by the producer's rule (extract.py:211-228) and whose unit is not list/table (extract.py:650), i.e. the rows that census_field_rows (237-255) hands to the section builder; the slug is computed with the producer's _slug (927-928). exact_matches = those whose slug, inside its own section, equals the slug of no other field row of that section (all field rows of the section counted, including non-scalar ones), so slug -> field name inside (section code, slug) has exactly one answer. collisions = sections with two field rows of equal slug (0). The column index .c<n> is a value-column of the PDF row, not in the census, and is not needed for the field name. Not measured: a served vendor answer (no live request is allowed here), so whether the deployed producer's census is this file is not established by this read.
